question: Do the three required mutants (stratification, unclosed-slice guard, per-agent normalization) each die on their own assert, rather than converging on one?
method: Committed the real script and test first (commits 132e092, cb41a59 on this branch), then applied each mutation as an uncommitted one-line edit on top of that committed state, ran scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1, recorded which assert fired and the exit code, then reverted with 'git checkout -- scripts/token-budget-report.ps1' before applying the next mutation - never two mutants uncommitted at once.
Control run after each revert confirmed scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1 is green again on the unmutated committed state, so a failure could only be attributed to the mutation just applied.

mutants.description: Stratification collapses into one bucket: every classified subagent becomes "writer", review population goes to zero.
mutants.assertMessage: CHECK A (stratification) FAILED: writer=127 review=0 - both populations must be non-empty on the 2026-07-26..2026-08-05 slice (documented: 47 writer / 80 review). A zero here means the classifier put every subagent into one bucket.

mutants.description: The unclosed-slice guard is disabled outright.

change.to:

    if ($false) {

mutants.assertMessage: CHECK B (unclosed-slice guard) FAILED: -To 2026-08-06 with -Now 2026-08-07 (one closed day of margin, not two) exited 0 instead of refusing. This exact slice measured 87.99% vs 86.85% opus share a few hours apart on PR #291 (evidence/283-model-share.json, evidence/303-unclosed-slice-refusal.json).
mutants.assertLocation: scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1, Check B (refusal exit code and REFUSED_UNCLOSED_SLICE marker) - a different mechanism from A and C: it inspects the exit code/stderr of a fresh child-process invocation, not a field in the parsed JSON result

mutants.description: Per-agent normalization for writer cache-read is swapped back to the raw sum (division dropped for one field).
mutants.assertMessage: CHECK C (per-agent normalization) FAILED: writer perAgent.cacheReadTokens = 3587475367, but total(3587475367) / agentCount(47) = 76329263.1276596 (diff 3511146103.87234 > tolerance 76329.2631276596). CHECK C (per-agent normalization) FAILED: writer perAgent.cacheReadTokens (3587475367) is within 1% of the raw total (3587475367) with agentCount=47 - looks like the raw sum was returned unchanged instead of being divided by the agent count.
mutants.assertLocation: scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1, Check C (perAgent equals total/agentCount, and perAgent is materially smaller than the raw total)

summary: All three mutants turn scripts/test-token-budget-report.ps1 red, each on its own check (A, B, C) with a distinct assert message and, for B, a distinct code path (exit code / stderr of a fresh process) versus A and C (fields of one parsed JSON result). No two mutants died on the same assert.
